Document: Practice Direction 54D – Planning Court Claims
Part 2 of 3
==================================================
## Failure to file the acknowledgment of service

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Failure to file the acknowledgment of service] 4.21 Where a person served with the claim form has failed to file an acknowledgment of service in accordance with paragraphs 4.12 to 4.18, rule 8.4 does not apply and that person—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Failure to file the acknowledgment of service] (a)may not take part in a hearing to decide whether permission should be given unless the court allows him to do so; but

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Failure to file the acknowledgment of service] (b)provided that person complies with paragraphs 4.37 to 4.39 or any other direction of the court regarding the filing and service of—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Failure to file the acknowledgment of service] (i)detailed grounds for contesting the claim or supporting it on additional grounds; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Failure to file the acknowledgment of service] (ii)any written evidence, may take part in the hearing of the planning statutory review. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Failure to file the acknowledgment of service] 4.22 Where that person takes part in the hearing of the planning statutory review, the court may take the failure to file an acknowledgment of service into account when deciding what order to make about costs. ## Permission decision without a hearing

## 4.23 The court will generally consider the question of permission without a hearing. ## 4.24 Paragraphs 4.25 to 4.30 apply where the court, without a hearing—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.24 Paragraphs 4.25 to 4.30 apply where the court, without a hearing—] (a)refuses permission to proceed; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.24 Paragraphs 4.25 to 4.30 apply where the court, without a hearing—] (b)gives permission to proceed—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.24 Paragraphs 4.25 to 4.30 apply where the court, without a hearing—] (i)subject to conditions; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.24 Paragraphs 4.25 to 4.30 apply where the court, without a hearing—] (ii)on certain grounds only. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.24 Paragraphs 4.25 to 4.30 apply where the court, without a hearing—] 4.25 The court will serve its reasons for making the decision when it serves the order giving or refusing permission in accordance with paragraph 4.33. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.24 Paragraphs 4.25 to 4.30 apply where the court, without a hearing—] 4.26 Subject to paragraph 4.28, the claimant may not appeal but may request the decision to be reconsidered at a hearing. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.24 Paragraphs 4.25 to 4.30 apply where the court, without a hearing—] 4.27A request under paragraph 4.26 must be filed within 7 days after service of the reasons under paragraph 4.25. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.24 Paragraphs 4.25 to 4.30 apply where the court, without a hearing—] 4.28 The claimant, defendant and any other person who has filed an acknowledgment of service will be given at least 2 days’ notice of the hearing date. ## 4.29 The court may give directions requiring the proceedings to be heard by a Divisional Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.29 The court may give directions requiring the proceedings to be heard by a Divisional Court.] 4.30 Where the court refuses permission to proceed and records the fact that the application is totally without merit in accordance with rule 23.12, the claimant may not request that decision to be reconsidered at a hearing. ## Permission hearing

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Permission hearing] 4.31 Neither the defendant nor any other person need attend a hearing on the question of permission unless the court directs otherwise. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Permission hearing] 4.32 Where the defendant or any party does attend a hearing, the court will not generally make an order for costs against the claimant. ## Permission given

## 4.33 Where permission to proceed is given the court may also give directions. ## 4.34 Directions under paragraph 4.33 may include—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.34 Directions under paragraph 4.33 may include—] (a)a stay of proceedings to which the claim relates;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.34 Directions under paragraph 4.33 may include—] (b)directions requiring the proceedings to be heard by a Divisional Court; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.34 Directions under paragraph 4.33 may include—] (c)directions about serving the claim form and any evidence on other persons. ## Service of order giving or refusing permission

## 4.35 The court will serve—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.35 The court will serve—] (a)the order giving or refusing permission; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.35 The court will serve—] (b)any directions,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.35 The court will serve—] on—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.35 The court will serve—] (i)the claimant;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.35 The court will serve—] (ii)the defendant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.35 The court will serve—] (iii)  any other person who filed an acknowledgment of service. ## Defendant etc may not apply to set aside

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Defendant etc may not apply to set aside] 4.36 Neither the defendant nor any other person served with the claim form may apply to set aside an order giving permission to proceed. ## Response

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Response] 4.37 A defendant and any other person served with the claim form who wishes to contest the claim or support it on additional grounds must file and serve—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Response] (a)detailed grounds for contesting the claim or supporting it on additional grounds; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Response] (b)any written evidence, within 35 days after service of the order giving permission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Response] 4.38 Where the party filing the detailed grounds intends to rely on documents not already filed, that party must file a paginated bundle of those documents when filing the detailed grounds. ## 4.39 The following rules do not apply—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.39 The following rules do not apply—] (a)rule 8.5(3) and 8.5(4) (defendant to file and serve written evidence at the same time as acknowledgment of service); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.39 The following rules do not apply—] (b)rule 8.5(5) and 8.5(6) (claimant to file and serve any reply within 14 days). ## Where claimant seeks to rely on additional grounds

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Where claimant seeks to rely on additional grounds] 4.40 Where the claimant intends to apply to rely on additional grounds at the hearing of the planning statutory review, the claimant must give notice to the court and to any other person served with the claim form no later than 7 clear days before the hearing. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Where claimant seeks to rely on additional grounds] 4.41 The court’s permission is required if a claimant seeks to rely on grounds other than those for which the claimant has been given permission to proceed. ## Evidence

## 4.42 Rule 8.6(1) does not apply. ## 4.43 No written evidence may be relied on unless—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.43 No written evidence may be relied on unless—] (a)it has been served in accordance with—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.43 No written evidence may be relied on unless—] (i)this Practice Direction; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.43 No written evidence may be relied on unless—] (ii)direction of the court; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.43 No written evidence may be relied on unless—] (b)the court gives permission. ## 4.44 Disclosure is not required unless the court orders otherwise. ## Skeleton arguments

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Skeleton arguments] 4.45 The claimant must file and serve a skeleton argument not less than 21 working days before the date of the hearing of the statutory review. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Skeleton arguments] 4.46 The defendant and any other party wishing to make representations at the hearing of the planning statutory review must file and serve a skeleton argument not less than 14 working days before the date of the hearing. ## 4.47 Skeleton arguments must contain—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.47 Skeleton arguments must contain—] (a)a time estimate for the complete hearing, including delivery of judgment;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.47 Skeleton arguments must contain—] (b)a list of issues;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.47 Skeleton arguments must contain—] (c)a list of the legal points to be taken (together with any relevant authorities with page references to the passages relied on);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.47 Skeleton arguments must contain—] (d)a chronology of events (with page references to the bundle of documents –  see paragraphs 4.48 to 4.49 below);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.47 Skeleton arguments must contain—] (e)a list of essential documents for the advance reading of the court (with page references to the passages relied on) (if different from that filed with the claim form) and a time estimate for that reading); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.47 Skeleton arguments must contain—] (f)a list of persons referred to. ## Bundle of documents at hearing stage

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Bundle of documents at hearing stage] 4.48 The claimant must file a paginated and indexed bundle of all relevant documents required for the hearing of the planning statutory review when filing the claimant’s skeleton argument. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Bundle of documents at hearing stage] 4.49 The bundle must also include those documents required by the defendant and any other party who is to make representations at the hearing. ## Planning statutory review may be decided without a hearing

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Planning statutory review may be decided without a hearing] 4.50 The court may decide the claim for planning statutory review without a hearing where all the parties agree. ## Agreed final order

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Agreed final order] 4.51 If the parties agree about the final order to be made in a claim for planning statutory review, the claimant must file at the court a document (with 2 copies) signed by all the parties setting out the terms of the proposed agreed order together with a short statement of the matters relied on as justifying the proposed agreed order and copies of any authorities or statutory provisions relied on. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > Agreed final order] 4.52 The court will consider the documents referred to in paragraph 4.51 and will make the order if satisfied that the order should be made. ## 4.53 If the court is not satisfied that the order should be made, a hearing date will be set. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 4.53 If the court is not satisfied that the order should be made, a hearing date will be set.] 4.54 Where the agreement relates to an order for costs only, the parties need only file a document signed by all the parties setting out the terms of the proposed order. ## SECTION V – APPLICATIONS TO QUASH CERTAIN ORDERS, SCHEMES, ETC

## 5.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (1) This section applies where the High Court has jurisdiction under any enactment, on the application of any person to quash or prohibit any—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (a)order, scheme, certificate or plan of;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (b)amendment or approval of a plan of;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (c)decision of;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (d)action on the part of, a Minister or government department. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (2) The jurisdiction shall be exercisable by a single judge of the King’s Bench Division. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] 5.2 The claim form must be filed at the Administrative Court and served within the time limited by the relevant enactment for making the application. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] 5.3 Subject to paragraph 5.5, the claim form must be served on the appropriate Minister or government department and on the person indicated in the following table. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to— a compulsory purchase order made by an authority   other than the appropriate Minister or government department; or a clearance order under the Housing Act 1985 | The authority who made that order. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to a scheme or order— to which Section 2 of the Highways Act 1980   applies; and which was made by an authority other than the Secretary   of State | The authority that made the scheme or order. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to a structure plan, local plan or other development plan within the meaning of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 | The local planning authority who prepared the plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to any decision or order, or any action on the part of a Minister of the Crown to which section 21 of the Land Compensation Act 1961 applies— | The authority directly concerned with such decision,   order or action; or if that authority is the applicant, on every   person who would, if he were aggrieved by the decision, order or action, be   entitled to apply to the High Court under section 21 of the Land Compensation   Act. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to a scheme to which Schedule 32 of the Local Government, Planning and Land Act 1980 applies | The body which adopted the scheme. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] a compulsory purchase order made by an authority   other than the appropriate Minister or government department; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] a clearance order under the Housing Act 1985

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] The authority who made that order. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to a scheme or order—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] to which Section 2 of the Highways Act 1980   applies; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] which was made by an authority other than the Secretary   of State

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] The authority that made the scheme or order. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to a structure plan, local plan or other development plan within the meaning of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] The local planning authority who prepared the plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to any decision or order, or any action on the part of a Minister of the Crown to which section 21 of the Land Compensation Act 1961 applies—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] The authority directly concerned with such decision,   order or action; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] if that authority is the applicant, on every   person who would, if he were aggrieved by the decision, order or action, be   entitled to apply to the High Court under section 21 of the Land Compensation   Act. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] If the application relates to a scheme to which Schedule 32 of the Local Government, Planning and Land Act 1980 applies

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] The body which adopted the scheme. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] 5.4 In paragraph 5.3, “the appropriate Minister or government department” means the Minister of the Crown or government department—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (a)by whom the order, scheme, certificate, plan, amendment, approval or decision in question was or may be made, authorised, confirmed, approved or given;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (b)on whose part the action in question was or may be taken. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] 5.5 Where the application relates to an order made under the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, the claim form must be served—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (a)if the order was made by a Minister of the Crown, on that Minister;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (b)if the order was made by a local authority with the consent, or following a direction, of a Minister of the Crown, on that authority and also on that Minister;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.1] (c)in any other case, on the local authority by whom the order was made. ## 5.6 Evidence at the hearing of an application under this paragraph is by witness statement. ## 5.7 The applicant must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.7 The applicant must—] (a)file a witness statement in support of the application in the Administrative Court within 14 days after service of the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.7 The applicant must—] (b)serve a copy of the witness statement and of any exhibit on the respondent at the time of filing. ## 5.8 The respondent must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.8 The respondent must—] (a)file any witness statement in opposition to the application in the Administrative Court within 21 days after service on him of the applicant’s witness statement; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.8 The respondent must—] (b)serve a copy of his witness statement and of any exhibit on the applicant at the time of filing. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.8 The respondent must—] 5.9 Unless the court otherwise orders, the application will not be heard earlier than 14 days after the time for filing a witness statement by the respondent has expired. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.8 The respondent must—] 5.10 Where an application is made under section 66 of the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 to question the validity of a public spaces protection order or of a variation of such an order—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.8 The respondent must—] (a)the claim form must be served on the local authority by which the order or variation was made or varied; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 5.8 The respondent must—] (b)paragraphs 5.1(2), 5.2 and 5.6 to 5.9 apply. ## SECTION VI – APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > SECTION VI – APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT] 6.1 An application for permission to appeal to the High Court under section 289 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (“the TCP Act”) or section 65 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 (“the PLBCA Act”) must be made within 28 days after notice of the decision is given to the applicant. ## 6.2 The application—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.2 The application—] (a)must be in writing and must set out the reasons why permission should be granted; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.2 The application—] (b)if the time for applying has expired, must include an application to extend the time for applying, and must set out the reasons why the application was not made within that time. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.2 The application—] 6.3 The applicant must, before filing the application, serve a copy of it on the persons referred to in paragraph 6.11 with the draft appellant’s notice and a copy of the witness statement or affidavit to be filed with the application. ## 6.4 The applicant must file the application in the Administrative Court Office with—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.4 The applicant must file the application in the Administrative Court Office with—] (a)a copy of the decision being appealed;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.4 The applicant must file the application in the Administrative Court Office with—] (b)draft appellant’s notice;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.4 The applicant must file the application in the Administrative Court Office with—] (c)a witness statement or affidavit verifying any facts relied on; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.4 The applicant must file the application in the Administrative Court Office with—] (d)a witness statement or affidavit giving the name and address of, and the place and date of service on, each person who has been served with the application. If any person who ought to be served has not been served, the witness statement or affidavit must state that fact and the reason why the person was not served. ## 6.5 An application will be heard—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.5 An application will be heard—] (a)by a single judge; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.5 An application will be heard—] (b)unless the court otherwise orders, not less than 21 days after it was filed at the Administrative Court Office. ## 6.6 Any person served with the application is entitled to appear and be heard. ## 6.7 Any respondent who intends to use a witness statement or affidavit at the hearing—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.7 Any respondent who intends to use a witness statement or affidavit at the hearing—] (a)must file it in the Administrative Court Office; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.7 Any respondent who intends to use a witness statement or affidavit at the hearing—] (b)must serve a copy on the applicant as soon as is practicable and in any event, unless the court otherwise allows, at least 2 days before the hearing. ## 6.8 The court may allow the applicant to use a further witness statement or affidavit. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.8 The court may allow the applicant to use a further witness statement or affidavit.] 6.9 Where on the hearing of an application the court is of the opinion that a person who ought to have been served has not been served, the court may adjourn the hearing, on such terms as it directs, in order that the application may be served on that person. ## 6.10 Where the court grants permission—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.10 Where the court grants permission—] (a)it may impose terms as to costs and as to giving security;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.10 Where the court grants permission—] (b)it may give directions; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.10 Where the court grants permission—] (c)the relevant appellant’s notice must be served and filed within 7 days of the grant. ## 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] (a)the Secretary of State;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] (b)the local planning authority who served the notice or gave the decision, as the case may be, or, where the appeal is brought by that authority, the appellant or applicant in the proceedings in which the decision appealed against was given;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] (c)in the case of an appeal brought by virtue of section 289(1) of the TCP Act or section 65(1) of the PLBCA Act, any other person having an interest in the land to which the notice relates; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] (d)in the case of an appeal brought by virtue of section 289(2) of the TCP Act, any other person on whom the notice to which those proceedings related was served. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] 6.12 The appeal will be heard and determined by a single judge unless the court directs that the matter be heard and determined by a Divisional Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] 6.13 The court may remit the matter to the Secretary of State to the extent necessary to enable the Secretary of State to provide the court with such further information in connection with the matter as the court may direct.
